correctness.rationale: For all integers m,n>=2 and real positive alpha,beta the weighted product metric has only two coordinate-edge types. The double-centering map R is an idempotent onto the zero-marginal subspace. Averaging an arbitrary projection over S_m x S_n yields the uniquely equivariant projection R, since any equivariant map from either one-coordinate subspace into U is zero. The dual Lipschitz calculation gives the upper bound 2 min(alpha,beta) max{(n-1)/(n alpha),(m-1)/(m beta)}, and two explicit 1-Lipschitz functions attain its two terms, establishing equality for all parameters. The norm-one thresholds follow by exhaustive comparisons alpha<=beta or beta<=alpha. Packaged edge-dual LP verifies 144 finite parameter instances but is not used to infer the universal theorem.

value.rationale: The interaction subspace is canonical in decomposing additive-coordinate and genuinely joint transportation fluctuations. Its minimum projection norm, rather than merely the norm of a convenient projection, is determined for every finite alphabet pair and every positive anisotropic weight pair. The theorem identifies a sharp binary-factor contractivity phase boundary and proves the impossibility of contractive complementability for all nonbinary pairs, a structural classification with direct relevance to product metric decompositions.
